subject: Human Evolution
title: Genetic Maps of Migration
description: A quick, practical guide to Genetic Maps of Migration.

hook.text: Plot genetic similarity on a map and you see streams: trails of ancestry flowing across continents.

buildup.text: Principal component analysis of DNA clusters people geographically—your genes reflect where your ancestors lived.

discovery.text: Genetic maps closely mirror geography because nearby populations exchanged genes more often than distant ones.

twist.text: But migrations disrupt the pattern. The Romani, Ashkenazi Jews, and Bantu speakers show long-range genetic links.

climax.text: Genetic geography reveals both isolation and connection—every population is a palimpsest of ancient movements.

punchline.text: Your DNA is a map of everywhere your ancestors went.

quiz.question: Why do genetic maps often mirror geography?
options: Nearby populations exchanged genes more frequently than distant ones
